explain.say: A steady reactor needs each fission to cause, on average, exactly one more. Control rods containing elements like boron or cadmium soak up spare neutrons, so the chain cannot grow.

faq.q: What are control rods made of?
faq.a: They contain elements that absorb neutrons very strongly, such as boron, cadmium, silver, indium or hafnium. These atoms swallow neutrons without splitting, taking them out of the chain.
asks: Why is boron used in control rods?

faq.q: How do control rods change a reactor's power?
faq.a: More rod in the core means more neutrons absorbed and fewer fissions, so less heat. Pulling the rods out lets more neutrons survive to cause fissions, raising the power.
asks: How do you turn a reactor up or down?

faq.q: What does the moderator do in a reactor?
faq.a: Neutrons from fission are very fast, and uranium-235 catches slow ones far better. The moderator, usually water or graphite, slows them down as they bounce off its light atoms.

faq.q: What happens if a reactor gets too hot?
faq.a: In water-cooled reactors, hotter water becomes less dense and slows neutrons less well, so fewer fissions happen and the power falls by itself. Engineers call this negative feedback.

A scram is an emergency shutdown in which all the control rods go fully into the core at once. It stops the chain reaction in seconds, but the fuel still needs cooling because its radioactive products keep making heat.
asks: How do you shut down a nuclear reactor?

facts: Just after shutdown, reactor fuel still produces about 6 to 7 percent of its full power as decay heat, falling quickly over the following hours.
Pressurised water reactors also dissolve boron in their cooling water to help control the reaction.

quiz.say: An operator lowers the control rods further into the core. What happens?
quiz.show: Lowering the control rods makes the power…

options.show: Fall, because more neutrons are absorbed
options.say: Fall, because more neutrons are absorbed

options.show: Rise, because the rods add fuel
options.say: Rise, because the rods add fuel

quiz.why: Control rods absorb neutrons, so pushing them in leaves fewer neutrons to cause fission.

wrong.1: Control rods contain no fuel; they absorb neutrons.
wrong.2: Moving the rods is exactly how the power is changed.
